title: Compact-support exchange into the chosen compactification
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $n\geq1$, and put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the small pro-etale sites and the derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)=D(\Sh(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A))$ of sheaves of modules over the constant sheaf of rings $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the same categories as in [pur713-def-shriek-exchange] and [def-weil-extension-by-zero], and their ordinary unbounded pullbacks and direct images [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with the canonical identifications $u^{-1}A_V\cong A_U$ of the constant coefficient sheaves. Let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$
be a Cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f$ separated of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Choose compactifications $c_f=(j,p)$ of $f$ and $c_{f'}=(j_{f'},p_{f'})$ of $f'$; a compactification of $h$ means a factorization $h=r i$ with $i$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $r$ proper [def-nagata-compactification]. Let $c'=(j',p')$ be the base change of $c_f$ [pur713-def-base-changed-compactification]. For any of these compactifications $d=(i,r)$ write $R_{d,A}=Rr_{*,A}\mathrm D(i_{!,A})$, where $\mathrm D(i_{!,A})$ is induced by applying the exact extension-by-zero functor [def-weil-extension-by-zero, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero] termwise and using its factorization through the derived localizations [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]; set $Rf_{!,A}=R_{c_f,A}$ and $Rf'_{!,A}=R_{c_{f'},A}$.

Assume the comparison input named “Comparison of compactifications, finite coefficients” in the source, namely a specified natural isomorphism
$$
\theta_{c',A}:R_{c',A}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{c_{f'},A}=Rf'_{!,A}
$$
on $D(X'_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. This is supplied comparison data, rather than an assertion here that such an isomorphism exists on the entire ambient category. Let
$$
\operatorname{Ex}_{!,\square,A}:Lg_A^*Rf_{!,A}\longrightarrow R_{c',A}Lg'^*_A
$$
be the auxiliary-compactification exchange of [pur713-def-shriek-exchange]. Define the compact-support exchange into the chosen compactification by
$$
\operatorname{Ex}^{\circ}_{!,\square,A}
:=(\theta_{c',A}Lg'^*_A)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{!,\square,A}:
Lg_A^*Rf_{!,A}\longrightarrow Rf'_{!,A}Lg'^*_A.
$$
This is a natural transformation of functors $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to D(Y'_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. At every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ its component is invertible if and only if $\operatorname{Ex}_{!,\square,A,K}$ is invertible, because $\theta_{c',A,Lg'^*_AK}$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $F=Lg_A^*Rf_{!,A}$, $G=R_{c',A}Lg'_A^*$ and $H=Rf'_{!,A}Lg'_A^*$. The current statement of [pur713-def-shriek-exchange] defines $Rf_{!,A}=Rp_{*,A}\mathrm D(j_{!,A})$ and $R_{c',A}=Rp'_{*,A}\mathrm D(j'_{!,A})$ on the full unbounded pro-etale derived categories and supplies the auxiliary natural transformation $\alpha:F\to G$ between these composites. These are exactly the functors used here, with the base-changed compactification $c'$ as the auxiliary target. The comparison input supplies $\theta:R_{c',A}\cong Rf'_{!,A}$, so its component $t_K=\theta_{Lg'_A^*K}$ has source $G(K)$ and target $H(K)$. Define $\beta_K=t_K\alpha_K$. For $a:K\to L$, naturality gives $H(a)\beta_K=H(a)t_K\alpha_K=t_LG(a)\alpha_K=t_L\alpha_LF(a)=\beta_LF(a)$. Thus these components define exactly the displayed natural transformation.

proof.text: For a fixed $K$, write $\alpha=\operatorname{Ex}_{!,\square,A,K}$ and $t=\theta_{c',A,Lg'_A^*K}$, so $\beta=t\alpha$, with $\alpha:F(K)\to G(K)$ and $t:G(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(K)$ as in step 1. If $\alpha$ is invertible, the map $s=\alpha^{-1}t^{-1}$ satisfies $s\beta=\alpha^{-1}t^{-1}t\alpha=1_{F(K)}$ and $\beta s=t\alpha\alpha^{-1}t^{-1}=1_{H(K)}$. Conversely, if $\beta$ is invertible, put $r=\beta^{-1}t$. Then $r\alpha=\beta^{-1}t\alpha=\beta^{-1}\beta=1_{F(K)}$ and $\alpha r=t^{-1}\beta\beta^{-1}t=1_{G(K)}$, using $\alpha=t^{-1}\beta$. Thus $r$ is inverse to $\alpha$, proving both directions.
